Title: Prize winners for the eNews survey
NewsSummary: Prize winners for the eNews survey
NewsContent:
Dear Readers,

Thank you for your enthusiastic response to our eNews survey and for sharing your insights with us. 

Your feedback has always been important and has enabled significant improvements to the content and design of this newsletter since its launch in November 2013.

In the year ahead, we will continue to work towards building a sense of community across AKU by sharing updates about the inspiring initiatives you and your colleagues have taken. In line with your feedback, we hope to add features on the following topics:

  • Student, alumni, faculty and staff success stories
  • What’s happening at AKU
  • Career advice from prominent alumni
  • AKU’s contribution to emergencies in the communities around it
  • AKU milestones​
Of course, since you already value updates about research developments, campus news and awards, these sections will continue to be a priority for the editorial team.

We’re also pleased to learn that 70 percent of you were satisfied with eNews’s content and that 94 percent of respondents believed that the layout was appealing.

Out of the 115 people who completed the survey, the 10 lucky winners of a free lunch have been informed by email. A few of the winners got in touch with the team and had this to say:

“I work in a clinical setting in Karachi...I would like to see more updates about new technologies and initiatives for better patient outcomes. Like the initiation of nursing navigator in Oncology.” - Laila Hussain.

“I would really like to commend the efforts of the team working on The Daily Media Summary and monthly eNews. I would only like to suggest one thing and that is if we can name e-News as eNews AKU.” – Yasmeen Mughal, Human Resources.

“For news about AKU I read the media summary, e-news and I read the noticeboards in the medical college. One thing I would like to see in eNews is stories about staff who are important to AKU’s operations such as housekeeping, maintenance and security.” - Irum, Oncology.

We’d like to share another important development with you. Since more readers than ever are reading eNews on mobile, we hope to introduce a mobile-friendly version of the newsletter very soon.

Whether you’re reading from Kampala, Kisumu, Kabul, Karachi, London, Nairobi or Dar, we hope to continue to share the key stories from the entire AKU family with you.

Thank you once again for your feedback. We will be in touch with more updates as we move towards the relaunch of your newsletter.

The eNews team​​
